title: Position and Location: Where Is It?
seo_title: Foundation Position Words Worksheets: Above, Under, Behind, Between (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Describe the position and location of themselves and objects in relation to other people and objects within a familiar space.
meta_desc: Free Foundation (Prep, Kindergarten) maths worksheets on position and location, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9MFSP02): above, under, next to, in front of, behind, on top of, between, first and last. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: Position words tell where something is.
key_sub: In front of is closer, behind is further away. Between is in the middle of two things.
body_html:
Position words

Position words tell where something is: above, under, next to, in front of, behind, on top of, inside, between, first and last.

In a line

The first one is at the start and the last one is at the end. Between means in the middle of two things.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Mixing up in front of and behindIn front is closer to you; behind is hidden or further away
Mixing up above and underAbove is higher up; under is lower down
Mixing up first and lastFirst is at the start of the line

faq.q: What position words do Foundation students learn?
faq.a: Words like above, under, next to, in front of, behind, on top of, inside, between, first and last, to describe where they and objects are (AC9MFSP02).

faq.q: Do Foundation students learn left and right?
faq.a: Left and right are introduced gently but are not the focus. Words like next to, between, in front of and behind come first.

faq.q: Why are position words part of maths?
faq.a: They are the start of geometry and maps. Later children use them to give directions, read grids and describe shapes.

faq.q: How can I practise at home?
faq.a: Play hide and seek with a toy and describe where it is, or give instructions: Put the cup next to the plate. Stand behind the chair.
